title: Simultaneous K-flat normalization of strict quotient expressions
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi$, and composable scheme morphisms $Z\xrightarrow hX\xrightarrow fY$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $W=Z,X,Y$ set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site, $R_W=\varprojlim_nB_{W,n}$, and write $q^W_{m,n}:B_{W,m}\to B_{W,n}$ for the quotient maps, for $m\geq n\geq1$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_r$ be any finite list, possibly empty, of integer-indexed K-flat complexes of $R_Y$-module sheaves with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

A finite expression here starts with the complexes $P_{i,n}=P_i\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,n}$ at $Y$ and the units $B_{W,n}[0]$ at each $W$, and applies finitely many direct-sum total tensors of two expressions on the same scheme [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and termwise module pullbacks along $f,h,f\circ h$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Denote its resulting complex at $W$ by $K_n$. Give the generators their actual quotient transitions, and give tensor and pullback expressions the induced semilinear transitions $t^K_{m,n}:K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$; scalar restriction is along $q^W_{m,n}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

Every such $K_n$ is K-flat with flat terms over $B_{W,n}$. Its localization computes the same expression with derived tensor and derived pullback [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The $t^K_{m,n}$ obey the identity and quotient cocycle strictly, so after restriction to $R_W$ they define a complex of strict towers. Their derived transition-adjoints
$$\alpha^K_{m,n}:K_m\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}\longrightarrow K_n$$
are represented on these very complexes by the ordinary tensor-adjoints of $t^K_{m,n}$ and are isomorphisms. For a generator $P_i$ this representative is
$$(P_i\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,m})\otimes_{B_{Y,m}}B_{Y,n}\longrightarrow P_i\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,n},\qquad (x\otimes b)\otimes a\longmapsto x\otimes q^Y_{m,n}(b)a,$$
with inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$; the unit case is the same multiplication formula. For a tensor expression its adjoint is the strong monoidal scalar-extension comparison followed by $\alpha^U_{m,n}\otimes^L\alpha^V_{m,n}$. For a pullback expression along $g:W'\to W$, its adjoint is $g^{-1}\alpha^U_{m,n}$ under the canonical scalar-change comparison and $g^{-1}B_{W,j}\cong B_{W',j}$ for $j=m,n$. Thus these particular strict expression towers are normalized coherent systems [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], with the adjoints of their actual transitions. No boundedness, constructibility or flatness of $q^W_{m,n}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0G7E (label lemma-pullback-K-flat) and 07A2 (label lemma-tensor-product-K-flat); agent-formulated simultaneous strict quotient-expression refinement of lem-pur-integral-coherence-tower, former proof step 1.

proof.text: For every arrow $g:W'\to W$ and every level $j$, use the constant-ring comparison $c^g_j:g^{-1}B_{W,j}\cong B_{W',j}$. It commutes with $q_{m,n}$: both composites send a constant section $b$ to its quotient $q_{m,n}(b)$, and the maps extend uniquely from the constant presheaf by sheafification. Fixed-coefficient module pullback is therefore exact inverse image with the action transported through $c^g_j$. Work on the compatible small representatives specified by the inverse-image definition. We prove the assertions simultaneously by structural induction on the finite expression: the induction claim includes flat terms, K-flatness, computation of derived operations, strict transition identities, and invertibility and the stated formulas for transition-adjoints. Distinct syntactic pullback expressions need not be identified with one another.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat, applied to pro-etale inverse images; constant coefficient identifications as cited

proof.text: For a generator $P_i$, apply change-of-rings preservation to $R_Y\to B_{Y,n}$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given K-flatness and flatness of every term of $P_i$, so $P_{i,n}$ is K-flat with flat terms. The derived change-of-rings theorem identifies its localization with $P_i\otimes^L_{R_Y}B_{Y,n}$. For a unit $B_{W,n}[0]$, tensoring any acyclic complex with the unit gives that same complex, so it is K-flat; its only nonzero term is free of rank one and the zero terms are flat. These are all base cases, including when the generator list is empty.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat, identity underlying topos; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change

proof.text: For a tensor expression $K_n=\operatorname{Tot}(U_n\otimes_{B_{W,n}}V_n)$, the induction hypotheses give flat-term K-flat factors. Apply the total-tensor model theorem: its conclusion gives K-flatness and flatness of every direct-sum total term, even for unbounded factors, and identifies its localization with $U_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}V_n$. Thus this new complex remains an eligible representative for every subsequent operation.

source.place: Tag 07A2, lemma-tensor-product-K-flat, and Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, proof

proof.text: For a pullback expression $K_n=g_n^*U_n$, apply the ringed-topos derived pullback/tensor theorem with coefficient rings $B_{W,n},B_{W',n}$ and coefficient map $c^g_n$. The induction hypothesis gives a K-flat input with flat terms. The theorem says its termwise pullback is again K-flat with flat terms and that applying pullback to this representative computes $Lg_n^*$. This proves the representative assertion at this induction step for each of $f,h,f\circ h$, without any flatness hypothesis on a quotient ring map.

The transitions are chain maps and satisfy the cocycle by a separate induction on the same expression. For a generator they send $x\otimes b$ to $x\otimes q_{m,n}(b)$; for a unit they are $q_{m,n}$. Hence the identity and cocycle follow from $q_{k,n}=q_{m,n}q_{k,m}$. For a tensor they send $u\otimes v$ to $t^U_{m,n}(u)\otimes t^V_{m,n}(v)$, which is balanced since both factors are semilinear for the same $q_{m,n}$. The two composite transitions agree on every pure tensor by the induction hypotheses, in each degree summand, hence on the sheafified total tensor. The differential $du\otimes v+(-1)^{\deg u}u\otimes dv$ is preserved. For a pullback the formula in scalar coordinates is $s\otimes u\mapsto q_{m,n}(s)\otimes g^{-1}t^U_{m,n}(u)$; balancing follows from the coefficient square in Step 1, and both composite formulas agree by the induction hypothesis and $q_{k,n}=q_{m,n}q_{k,m}$. All these maps commute with restriction of local sections. Finally $q_{m,n}\pi_m=\pi_n$ makes these transitions $R_W$-linear after scalar restriction. In each cochain degree they therefore give a strict tower, and their differentials give a complex of such towers.

source.place: Ordinary quotient maps, sheafified balanced tensor, and direct-sum total differential; definitions as cited

proof.text: At every expression and every $m\geq n$, the flat-term K-flatness already proved lets us use the representative-normalized derived coefficient adjunction for $q^W_{m,n}$. In its notation take $P=K_m$, $H=K_n$ and $g=t^K_{m,n}$. Clause (2) identifies the adjunct of the localized actual transition with the localization of the actual chain map $\bar t^K_{m,n}:K_m\otimes_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}\to K_n$, $z\otimes a\mapsto a\,t^K_{m,n}(z)$. It remains to prove that these maps are isomorphisms by structural induction, retaining this fixed representative of each adjunct.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, specialized to change of rings, with the representative normalization in the cited node

proof.text: For $K=P_i$, the map from Step 6 is $(x\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes q_{m,n}(b)a$. Its proposed inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$ respects $R_Y$-balancing because $q_{m,n}\pi_m=\pi_n$. The first composite fixes $x\otimes a$; the other sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes q_{m,n}(b)a=(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ by $B_{Y,m}$-balancing. They are chain maps since they leave $x$ and its differential unchanged. These sectionwise balanced maps induce inverse maps on the sheaf tensors. For $B_{W,m}[0]$, the same calculation is $b\otimes a\mapsto q_{m,n}(b)a$ with inverse $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. This proves the generator and unit adjoints are chain isomorphisms.

source.place: Balanced scalar-association calculation underlying Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition

proof.text: For $K=\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes V)$, apply the cochain pullback/tensor comparison to the identity underlying topos with ring map $q_{m,n}$. In right scalar coordinates its formula is $(u\otimes v)\otimes a\mapsto(u\otimes a)\otimes(v\otimes1)$, with inverse $(u\otimes a)\otimes(v\otimes b)\mapsto(u\otimes v)\otimes ab$. Follow it by $\bar t^U_{m,n}\otimes\bar t^V_{m,n}$. The result sends $(u\otimes v)\otimes a$ to $a\,t^U_{m,n}(u)\otimes t^V_{m,n}(v)$, exactly $\bar t^K_{m,n}$ from Step 6. The comparison is a chain isomorphism, and the two factor maps are chain isomorphisms by induction, so this map is an isomorphism. All complexes involved are flat-term K-flat by Steps 2–4 and change-of-rings preservation. The ringed-topos derived monoidal comparison is computed on these representatives, so after localization the displayed factorization is exactly the strong monoidal scalar-extension comparison followed by $\alpha^U_{m,n}\otimes^L\alpha^V_{m,n}$.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; explicit cochain comparison at the identity topos

proof.text: For $K=g^*U$, use the scalar comparison normalization with $A_Y=B_{W,m}$, $B_Y=B_{W,n}$ and inverse image $g^{-1}$, transporting its target rings by $c^g_m,c^g_n$. It gives the canonical chain isomorphism $(g_m^*U_m)\otimes_{B_{W',m}}B_{W',n}\cong g_n^*(U_m\otimes_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n})$, compatible with $u\mapsto u\otimes1$, and identifies its localization with the canonical derived scalar-change comparison. In the inverse-image coordinates of Step 1 it sends $g^{-1}u\otimes a$ to $a\,(g^{-1}u\otimes1)$. Composing with $g_n^*\bar t^U_{m,n}$ gives $a\,g^{-1}t^U_{m,n}(u)$, precisely the adjunct of the induced transition. Equivalently, precomposing with the insertion $z\mapsto z\otimes1$ gives $t^K_{m,n}$, which uniquely determines its ordinary adjunct. The induction hypothesis and functoriality make this composite a chain isomorphism. Its localization is therefore $g^{-1}\alpha^U_{m,n}$ under the stated scalar-change comparison, proving the pullback induction step for the actual maps.

source.place: Tag 03EL, sites-modules-lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Tag 0G7E and Tag 07A6; scalar-change mate normalization in the cited node

proof.text: Structural induction has now proved every asserted property for each finite expression. The complex of strict $R_W$-towers constructed in Step 5 localizes to the coherent derived-tower datum required in the normalized DVR tower definition; evaluation gives the scalar restrictions of $QK_n$ with precisely the localized transitions from that step. Step 6 identifies their derived adjoints, and Steps 7–9 make those adjoints isomorphisms. The identity and cocycle equations are already strict before localization, so all parts of that definition hold. The argument used only the given flat terms and K-flatness, and the existing unbounded stability theorems. The empty generator list, zero generators, and $m=n$ are included; at $m=n$ the adjunct is the usual action unitor. No claim about preserving an inverse limit by $g^{-1}$ was used.
